cells.tense: The curiosity is on the tongue now and it has somewhere to land.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Something you are tending has been hovering. Make that call and do the single thing it asks for, without rehearsing it once it's done.
cells.core:
Something near you is still forming, and the asking happens in your presence. You carry questions with nothing settled behind them, so the ones nearby wonder instead of guessing. A thing gets to stay unfinished a day longer, because the next honest question is worth more than a tidy answer.

The balance is free to feed a decision next. Pick what you are tending that has been hovering, make the call, and do the one thing it needs. The cost is the ease of not deciding yet. What grows around someone who can choose without ceremony learns that a direction is a thing you pick up and act on — and nothing growing needs the reasons spread out first.
cells.sheetLine: You leave things unfinished because the next real question is worth more.
cells.verb: Turn over every stone with the energy of finding out
cells.place: Where something is still forming and no one is forcing it

cells.tense: Every stone will be turned before anything has been allowed to set.
cells.act: explore a direction before it has a destination
cells.ask: Give a week to a direction that draws you and keep it nameless — follow where it goes before you say what it is for.
cells.core:
Where something is growing, the asking has outrun the thing itself. The next question arrives before the last one lands, and the pace of your wondering starts to get set for what is still forming rather than by it. Curiosity that ought to serve the growing thing has begun to hurry it.

The balance is free to feed the wondering side: time with a direction that draws you, before you decide what it is for. Keep it unnamed. Some things grow toward what you picked and some grow on their own, and a stretch of not declaring tells you which you have. Nothing you tend is hurt by your not having worked out yet where it goes.
cells.sheetLine: The questions arrive before anything has had a chance to settle.
cells.verb: Turn over every stone with the energy of finding out

cells.tense: The question was left at the door, and the door is already behind the room.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Picture for a little while what something you tend looks like a step further on — then take that step before the day is out.
cells.core:
Where something is growing, the curiosity has gone quiet. You used to turn things over as a way of being near them; now the wondering happens at a distance, when it happens at all, and what you are tending gets fed on routine instead of interest. You are still nearby. The asking stopped, and its absence has a shape.

The balance is free to feed the picturing. Sit with what a step further on would look like for something you tend, see it fully enough to feel toward it, then take that step today. No need to feel curious first. Picturing comes before interest, and interest tends to arrive once the next step has somewhere to be. What you are growing waits on the smaller of the two.

cells.tense: The weighing between you and what you tend is going on while you call it patience.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Look once at something you are tending and check whether the time it takes costs more than it returns — then act on what you find.
cells.core:
You keep what is growing on an even keel, quietly adjusting what you give to match what it can take, and your account of it is that you are patient. There is a keeper in this, keeping accounts. The keeper's story is the story of someone waiting; the ones who lean on you have not believed that story once, and they don't need to.

The balance is free to feed the fair look. Give an honest round of weighing to something you tend — what it asks against what it gives back — and act on the answer. The cost is giving up the story that you are only waiting. Fair attention is not the same as endless tending, and the thing you tend already knows the difference.
cells.sheetLine: The patience has a keeper, and the keeper is keeping accounts.
cells.verb: Turn over every stone with the energy of finding out
cells.place: Where something is still forming and no one is forcing it

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is the Too Much cell's implication that the person's questioning has turned outward and is being aimed at what is growing near them, pressing for answers before a thing has formed — the record shows the excess of inquiry, not that it has found a target. A reader could reasonably say it is still private, still their own head, not yet landing on anyone; the ask (explore a direction a week before deciding what it is for) survives that being wrong, because it requires nothing from anyone. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'the questions are aimed at something now' — it is vivid, and it claims a location the record does not support.
